newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha finishes flat as Egypt tender closes.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha finishes flat as Egypt tender closes.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices were steadier on Wednesday after Tuesday's sharp falls and traders said much of the discussion was over the closure today of the latest tender issued by the state-owned Egyptian General Petroleum Company (EGPC,) traders said.

The tender, which closed in the afternoon, was for six months' worth of naphtha out of Suez and Alexandria and while exact quantities were not specified, dealers said it would be for around five cargoes a month from each port.
Traders said they did not know when the tender would be awarded but said offers would be treated as valid up until June 12.
"It has been very quiet but the EGPC tenders have concentrated everyone's mind," a trader at a U.K. refinery said.
June naphtha swaps were heard to have been traded at $189 a tonne cif NWE and physical numbers for full-range material were pegged in the vicinity of the June swaps.
